answer: Staggered heartbeat admission gate: each new agent identity must emit randomized check-ins across a 72-hour window, and burst-created identities are held until their timing diverges. Enforcement compares each identity's arrival curve against a mirror of expected jitter and throttles any cluster that rises like a single vine from one source. The per-identity cost is three days of spaced compute plus unique bandwidth per heartbeat, so an attacker cannot cheaply reach the summit of many active identities at once.
